title: Minimally Invasive Steering of Language Models
claim: A frozen model is steered at inference by optimizing additive vectors against reward while a regularizer limits deviation from the reference.
layout: 1 panel, bottom-to-top data flow, outer feedback loop arrow across top
description: A single block diagram showing data flowing bottom to top. Prompt and generation tokens (x_1…x_n, y_1…y_{m-1}) at the bottom feed a yellow, snowflake-marked Model Backbone, which outputs final-layer embeddings h_1…h_m. Green boxes u_1…u_m are added to each h_t through circled plus nodes. The sums enter a yellow, frozen LM Head, which outputs next-token distributions q_1…q_m drawn as small blue histograms. On the right, a red trapezoid labeled Fisher Regularizer and a green trapezoid labeled Reward Model feed a blue Gradient Update box. That box outputs updated vectors (u_1^+…u_m^+). A large light-blue arrow across the top, labeled 'New rollout with new steering vectors', loops back to the steering vectors. Pale labels on the left name each layer. The eye goes first to the central stacked model blocks and then to the loop arrow.
caption: Minimally invasive test-time steering. The transformer backbone and LM head (W, b) remain frozen. At each generation position t, MISVO adds a steering vector ut to the pre-logit hidden state ht, thereby modifying the next-token distribution. The steering vectors are optimized at inference time to increase reward while a Fisher-quadratic penalty controls the distributional deviation from the reference policy.
abstract: Test-time alignment adapts large language models (LLMs) to runtime objectives without updating model parameters. Pre-logit steering offers a lightweight approach by optimizing additive interventions to the hidden states of a frozen LLM, but excessive steering can distort output distributions and degrade generation quality. We propose Minimally Invasive Steering Vector Optimization (MISVO), which improves reward while controlling deviation from the reference policy. Rather than penalizing the Euclidean norm of steering vectors, we derive a quadratic regularizer from the local Kullback--Leibler (KL) geometry of the induced token distributions. The resulting Fisher-information penalty captures the distributional sensitivity of steering directions and admits an analytic gradient computed through matrix--vector products with the frozen language-model head. We further derive an exact decomposition of the sequence-level KL gradient and establish explicit, non-asymptotic bounds on the approximation errors, including the omitted trajectory-dependent score-function term. These results show that the frozen Fisher regularizer gradient approximates the full sequence-level KL gradient to first order in the steering magnitude. Across preference and code-generation tasks on four LLMs spanning approximately 1B--14B parameters, MISVO achieves the highest mean best-so-far reward in six of seven model--task settings, while maintaining diversity and coherence scores comparable to Best-of-$N$.
